Change ID: `220a8-enh envision-future-exploration-single-document`
Change Status: `implementing`
Owner: Engineering
Status: active
Last verified: 2026-10-30
Wave: 220a9 envision-future-exploration

## Rationale

The operator is trying Envision in real projects after local build 1.39.0+q02v. Tensorwell's author reports that capability validation corrected factual mistakes and reviews improved the roadmap, but personal infrastructure became the recommended destination before other futures received comparable exploration. A per-user deployment became a strategic anchor; broader organizational inference was bundled with a general agent platform and discounted for demand uncertainty that also affected the favored option. The author acknowledges inadequate execution of existing guidance. This is one reported field case, not independently reproduced evidence of universal failure or proof that a larger destination is better.

The operator also finds separate vision, research and review documents burdensome. The desired default is one readable vision and roadmap, with consequential research supporting its argument and review accounting in the response. The current seed defaults review evidence to a sibling and permits a separate research file. The operator also selected phased load

ing within this wave: a short always-read strategic core, with procedural detail read at its point of use. This tests an attention-management hypothesis; neither shorter text nor file separation alone proves improved adherence.

Solaris has now reported a second field run on 1.39.0+q02v, using Claude Code rather than the Tensorwell run's Codex host. Its author again developed one destination concretely and left others as labels; inferred local-first, lighting-only and ecosystem limits became strategic boundaries. An accurate capability inventory was misrepresented in the draft as missing functionality. All four review follow-ups reportedly found additional issues, followed by author edits to a final revision none had reviewed. Single-document delivery was explicitly requested and mostly worked; it is not evidence for the old default. These reports strengthen the motivation but remain author self-assessments, not independent artifact audits or a controlled cross-host comparison. Teton remains reserved for the next iteration.

## Product Intent

Help product owners discover a valuable, ambitious future and understand how to make it real. Before: the author can favor a polished extrapolation of today's implementation and split its reasoning across files. After: when the destination is open, a reader can explain serious alternative futures and why one is recommended, distinguish initial deployment from chosen product responsibility, and use one coherent document to understand the destination, useful horizons and immediate advances. The author receives a focused strategic core and reads applicable phase guidance before acting, rather than loading every procedural branch at entry. An operator-chosen destination remains authoritative; bigger is not automatically better.

This supports the adopted Wavefoundry vision's [H3 intent-to-work outcome](../../../VISION.md#horizon-3--executable-intent-and-sustained-missions) and [H4 exploration of materially different approa

ches](../../../VISION.md#horizon-4--competing-solutions-and-coordinated-engineering). It improves authoring foundations, not autonomous execution or those horizons' completion. The opening, roadmap overview and relevant horizon passages were consulted; they introduce no prerequisite authorizing broader runtime work. AC-2 and AC-3 test the user outcome; AC-1/4/5 test instruction delivery, strategic review and compatibility.

## Requirements

1. **Distinguish origin, starting point and possible destination.** Separate the problem that started the project, operator-established commitments, current implementation/deployment choices, deferred capabilities and proposed changes of product responsibility. Explicit current requirements remain binding until changed; neither dismiss them as accidents nor silently make them permanent limits. Name obligations introduced by a scope expansion and expose consequential choices to the operator. The first beneficiary or deployment need not define eventual reach.
2. **Explore fairly before recommending an open destination.** Before drafting the recommended destination, develop each serious alternative through a comparably concrete beneficiary experience, distinctive value, consequential obligations and uncertainties. This is an authoring sequence, not a requirement to put alternatives before the summary in the delivered vision. Compare product futures, not only engines or implementation methods. Explain the recommendation and sacrifices; apply missing and contrary evidence consistently to the favored option too. Comparable attention does not mean equal length, exhaustive research, a fixed option count or an invented optimum. Do not manufacture strategic alternatives when the operator has chosen the destination. Where ambition is requested, seriously examine transformative capacity beyond the backlog without imposing enterprise, cloud, autonomous-agent or platform scope. Do not assume commercialization is the objective: personal us

efulness, open contribution, adoption, financial return and other value can support different futures. Distinguish a product purpose from a distribution route or business model; options should differ in beneficiary experience or responsibility, not merely packaging.\n3. **Make consequential inference visible without new ceremony.** Place inferred beneficiary/scope/destination choices near the recommendation, with their implications and unresolved decisions. Silence is not selection. Continue legitimate provisional work; use the existing combined briefing for genuine blockers. Do not require the operator to choose a market before Envision helps explore it. Reuse concrete operator or beneficiary experience where available; ask for a decision-relevant missing example rather than inventing daily use or adding a mandatory interview. Personal usefulness, open adoption and income may coexist; a hobby or small team constrains pace without automatically capping the destination. Treat an interesting reviewer hypothesis as a hypothesis until supported or selected. Preserve useful horizons, technical and nontechnical dependencies, intermediate value, endurance, adaptability and lower precision at distance.\n4. **One coherent vision by default.** Write the existing canonical vision or root VISION.md; keep full review accounting in the final response. Retain a compact one- or two-line status in the vision naming the review date, reviewed revision or revisions, roles actually run, and pending finding count and unreviewed changes (or explicitly unknown/not reviewed). The status must distinguish the delivered content from the reviewed content without implying adoption or approval of subsequent edits. Integrate decision-relevant research conclusions, citations, enduring assumptions, contrary evidence and open strategic choices into the argument. A concise appendix is optional when useful. Do not concatenate research notes and review transcripts into a giant document or bury all evide

nce in an appendix. Consolidate general authorization/adoption/evidence caveats while retaining specific limits where a decision depends on them. A concise account of the operative brief belongs in the argument where it explains consequential choices; preserve the operator's meaning without requiring a verbatim interview transcript. Research limitations that affect those choices and the compact review status remain in the vision; full reviewer chronology and detailed revision coverage belong in the delivery response. No word ceiling on visions.\n5. **Preserve artifacts and explicit exceptions.** An explicit project/operator evidence-location instruction overrides the new default. Substantial separately reusable research may justify a companion: state its concrete purpose before creating it and honor a single-document request. Existing vision-output siblings do not automatically authorize new output files, deletion, overwrite or silent invalidation. On an authorized revision, incorporate needed conclusions, preserve working references and report historical siblings left unchanged. Retirement or relocation requires operator direction and preservation of unique evidence/links. Read-only requests write nothing. The current change does not consolidate real-project vision files.\n6. **Sharpen existing strategic-review remits.** Product strategy and independent challenge examine uneven alternatives, asymmetric uncertainty, conflated scopes and deployment assumptions promoted to destiny. Assess recommendation quality and connection of immediate advances to the larger future. Preserve current stakes-based coverage, independence, bounded repair and affected-reviewer verification. Report consequential contributions honestly: a no-new-finding follow-up is verification, not proof of uselessness, convergence or efficacy. Give verification reviewers the identified revision, prior findings and actual changes as claims to verify, not predetermined accepted or resolved verdicts. Shar

ed author framing and model limitations remain disclosed. Add no chair, mandatory Council, survey, telemetry or recurring assessment to ordinary Envision runs.
7. **Preserve working contracts.** Retain current-capability classification and validation, attributed operator experience, authorized research and source distinctions, ambition protection, adoption ownership, unrelated-edit preservation, capability-limit reporting and artifact-only authority. No automatic implementation, lifecycle records, adoption, network expansion or environment changes. Carry verified capability classifications through synthesis into priorities; change an established classification only when new evidence supports it. Resolve consequential disagreements among inventory, draft, source and reviewer claims with targeted checks or explicit uncertainty, not another mandatory broad audit. Keep destination and credible roadmap core; avoid option worksheets and mandatory interviews.
8. **Deliver consistently to new and existing targets.** Update seed 179, the local prompt, architecture prose and changelog. Extend and exercise seed160's changed-Envision reconciliation against an old canonical prompt with compatible additions and an explicit local artifact-policy conflict. Preserve additions; surface conflict without overwrite. Upgrade must not run Envision or alter vision/evidence files. Keep the skill a thin pointer; do not duplicate the workflow in accurate catalogs/registry/generated skills. Replace or consolidate instructions rather than accumulate clauses. R10 sets the always-read core target; retain a roughly net-neutral target across the complete canonical guidance set, with no hard total ceiling. Report core, each companion, total guidance and corresponding local counts using the same method, and explain any growth, value retained and redundant material removed. Reviewers assess readability and retained contracts alongside behavioral evidence, without claiming unobserved improvement.
9.

**Make the verification boundary and final revision coverage explicit.** After the normal initial review, one bounded author repair and affected-reviewer verification, stop further author repairs and report remaining actionable findings/decisions under the existing stopping rule. Do not silently apply another round and present the result as reviewed. If later operator direction authorizes further edits, identify the new revision and which earlier findings or checks still support it; disclose unverified changes and any focused follow-up actually performed. A usable provisional document may have pending findings. This is a clarification of the existing bounded workflow, not a new approval gate or automatic review loop. Keep R4's compact status accurate at delivery, including after any explicitly authorized later edit. In the delivery response distinguish the final document from the versions each reviewer assessed; a selected role or earlier approval does not cover subsequent changes by implication.


10. **Load procedural guidance at its point of use.** Restructure seed179 and the local Envision prompt as an always-read core targeting approximately 2,000 words or fewer, with four internal phase companions: research/evidence, revision/preservation, advisory review, and delivery/adoption. This is a meaningful reduction of the entry surface, not a numeric ceiling on visions or the total guidance set; explain any deviation from the core target for reviewer judgment. Keep purpose, authority/read-only/adoption limits, output default, research authorization, preservation obligations, commitment-versus-deployment grounding, capability status, alternatives-before-recommendation and roadmap shape in the core. Put their detailed procedures in the relevant phase owner rather than duplicating them. At each applicable step, the core names the exact full project-relative local companion path and requires reading it before the dependent action: research before gathering/assessing

evidence, revision before revising an existing vision, review before briefing reviewers or repairing findings, delivery before final validation/status/adoption handoff. Do not eagerly load all companions; retain needed context and reread only when materially changed or unavailable. Core invariants apply even before a phase is loaded; a skipped/omitted review still has honest delivery coverage. Read-only work obeys the same authority boundary. Missing, unreadable or contradictory required guidance stops that dependent step with a concrete report; do not silently skip it, fabricate review coverage, fall back around project policy or run setup/upgrade automatically. Independent reviewers receive their applicable remit and necessary brief/evidence, not a second whole authoring workflow by rote.\n11. **Install and reconcile the complete guidance set.** Canonical companions live in `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/envision/{research,revision,review,delivery}.prompt.md`; project-owned counterparts live in `docs/prompts/agents/envision/` with matching names. Seed100 authors missing companions and core references without exposing helpers as public commands. Seed160 and the local upgrade prompt reconcile the core and companions as one instruction set, using retained old/new canonical text and project additions. Process added, modified or removed members of the explicitly named core/companion source set even when seed179 is unchanged; backfill missing companions through the existing missing-only path. Inspect instruction-set completeness on partial-install/retry rather than treating an unavailable prior diff as proof that nothing needs reconciliation. Preserve compatible customizations in moved clauses, including moving them into the corresponding local companion when safe. Stop affected conflicting or ambiguous merges explicitly; partial reconciliation is not completion, and old inline rules must not remain as a competing owner after a successful move. Repetition is stable. Pac

kaging and extraction must deliver all companions using existing mechanisms; no new loader, registry entry or public command is introduced. Upgrade neither runs Envision nor changes actual vision/review/research outputs. Local guidance companions are operating instructions, not the output siblings R4 removes by default.

## Scope

**Problem statement:** two reported runs show asymmetric exploration despite existing advice; a growing always-read prompt mixes strategy and procedural branches. Default evidence-file proliferation distracts from the argument, and Solaris exposes capability-status drift and unreviewed post-verification edits. Phased loading addresses entry-context burden as a testable mechanism, not a guaranteed strategy-quality improvement.

**Intended edits:**

- `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/179-envision-project.prompt.md` and `seeds/envision/{research,revision,review,delivery}.prompt.md` below the same framework root: short strategic core, explicit phase transitions and canonical detailed guidance; reconcile contradictory clauses rather than append a checklist.
- `docs/prompts/envision-project.prompt.md` and `docs/prompts/agents/envision/{research,revision,review,delivery}.prompt.md`: corresponding project-local core/companions, preserving metadata and project additions.
- `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/100-project-prompt-surface-bootstrap.prompt.md`: missing-only companion authoring and internal-only helper status.
- `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/160-upgrade-wavefoundry.prompt.md` and `docs/prompts/upgrade-wavefoundry.prompt.md`: whole-set reconciliation, companion-only changes, moved customizations, conflicts and partial completion.
- `.wavefoundry/framework/README.md`: compact reference to the Envision companion layout in its prompt documentation.
- `docs/architecture/data-and-control-flow.md`: Envision evidence placement and explicit exceptions.
- Root `CHANGELOG.md`: prospective Unreleased entry; preserve the existing 1.39.0 build re

cord.
- This plan and later admitted-wave evidence/normal lifecycle records. Retain unique evaluation proof compactly, not a permanent forest of routine reviewer reports.

**Protected/read-only:** seed050/public catalog and prompt-surface manifest; renderer registry/logic, generated skills, production Python scripts and checked-in tests; seed170/Plan change; Wave Council/Archetype Council protocols and workflow config; VERSION/pack manifest; real VISION.md and siblings, docs/visions; historical waves/evidence. If inspection finds a genuine delivery contradiction, amend the intended edits and obtain applicable readiness before expanding scope.

**Out of scope:** Tensorwell or Wavefoundry graph/service architecture, changing either product destination, scanner repairs, actual sibling retirement, new research infrastructure, reducing review defaults based solely on follow-ups finding no defects, official packaging/release, real-target install/upgrade, commit/push. Disposable candidate package/extraction probes and fixture reconciliation are in scope; no VERSION stamp or publication. No automatic runs in Solaris or Teton.

**Delivery feasibility evidence (planning, executed):** Guru exercised actual `build_pack.collect_files`/`write_manifest`, `upgrade_wavefoundry._compute_seed_diffs`/`_extract_feature_members`, and prompt-name/manifest validators on disposable fixtures. Nested `seeds/envision/*.prompt.md` additions/modifications were packaged, recorded and detected while unchanged seed179 was omitted. The selected `docs/prompts/agents/envision/*.prompt.md` paths passed the exercised validators without public manifest rows; a wrong-suffix control failed. Existing seed100's internal-body convention and seed160's core-only mapping were read directly. Complete source/probe/limits are retained in the wave's readiness-evidence.json under `phase_delivery_investigation_2026_10_30`. This establishes transport/detection feasibility, not full installation, agent merge comp

liance or author adherence; AC-5/6 supply candidate evidence. Use explicit file paths: `seed_get`'s disk fallback is nonrecursive and cannot be assumed to resolve nested companions by bare name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Canonical/local core and companions consistently implement R1–R11 without residual default sibling-file obligations or contradictory chosen-destination rules. Before source edits, preserve installed 1.39.0+q02v canonical/local inputs from baseline commit `8a351d49`; seed 179 matches SHA-256 `7119e1518e13ec846b978a08e992f47d712f46b2b981ee59f0f48588b38107ff`. overload without prescribing a future or penalizing justified detail. Inputs are frozen before candidate outputs. Evaluator, candidate author and first-stage reader are distinct contexts.

For AC-5, inspect and reuse the retained 21y6d reconciliation fixture where compatible, updating its input to this frozen baseline and adding the explicit local artifact-policy conflict and companion-only upgrade case. Run it against this candidate; historical passing results are not evidence for new guidance. Document any necessary fixture adaptation without changing seed160.

Initial batch: one matched current/candidate open-destination pair from separate authors; one candidate chosen-destination revision with existing artifacts and staged post-verification findings; one focused strategic-review exercise for AC-4 reusing a frozen control instead of another full vision. The chosen-destination continuation also checks an explicitly authorized later edit and truthful revision coverage; it does not start another authoring trial. Reuse outputs across ACs. Record review scope and actual execution: any trial-specific narrowing is explicit and does not establish full-default adherence. Do not automatically run full review ensembles for every synthetic case. Reuse these authoring trajectories for AC-6: retain observable tool-read/action order and instruction volumes, and add one bounded missing-reference continuation rather than another full vision. If the host cannot expose adequate read-order evidence, report the claim unproven; author recollection alone is insufficient. Freeze applicability and missing-reference controls with the other inputs. Successful reads alone do not establish use; pair them with the relevant capability, preservation, evidence and coverage outcomes. Mask review-status metadata in blind-reader copies while preserving originals for AC-3/4.

The reader first reconstructs neutrally labeled artifacts without prompt identities, review verdicts, scoring anchors o

r expected conclusions. Preserve those answers before supplying brief-based judging questions and controls; judge the pair before other scenarios and disclose shared context. Record every attempt, failure and repair, candidate identities and measured effort where available. Do not infer cost savings, cross-model robustness, customer demand or superiority from one pair. A baseline pass limits the claim; do not replace it with a favorable fixture.

Each batch has a predeclared stopping point. If a required outcome remains unproven at that point or a repair fails its focused recheck, stop and return evidence/options to the operator. Do not begin a second batch without explicit operator direction. Required lifecycle reviews and canonical framework qualification remain separate obligations.

Tensorwell is reported discovery and coached repair evidence, not held-out validation. Solaris is a current-version field observation with an explicit artifact override; it cannot establish the old default or a controlled comparison against another project. Its platform/distribution/API/health claims are not independently verified here and must not become generic Envision requirements. Reported task tokens and durations may include cumulative context; do not sum them into billing, wall time or comparative cost without a reliable measurement basis. Five thousand words alone does not prove excessive depth; assess whether the decision and roadmap are usable at the project's stakes. Teton is an optional later uncoached field observation, requiring availability and operator authorization, not a blocking implementation dependency. Report field discrepancies honestly. This feedback collection does not become mandatory for every Envision invocation.

Title: Envision Future Exploration

## Objective

Help product owners explore ambitious product futures fairly and receive one coherent vision with a credible, adaptable roadmap. Give authors a focused strategic core with procedural guidance loaded at its point of use and delivered consistently to new and existing projects. Preserve operator commitments and current capabilities, distinguish initial deployment from eventual responsibility, and report final-revision review coverage honestly. This wave revises Envision guidance only; it neither chooses a target project's strategy nor changes runtime or implementation authority.

Change Status: `implementing`

This supports R2/R3's distinction between product purpose and distribution: an App Store path should not become the primary objective without that choice. d independently of conditional commercialization work. A usage diary is an optional proposed investigation, not a new prerequisite. Shared primer framing is one signal; red-team closing reused its original context, not an extra independent vote.
